To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the children with reading disability who were matched with their reading-age peers on nonverbal ability (IQ) did not differ from their peers on the cognitive processes related to reading disability.

(1) successive processing is the most important cognitive variable related to reading ability, (2) attention is also related to reading ability in children of average nonver bal IQ, and (3) successive processing is related to reading ability even in children who are of average IQ or higher.
(1) children with reading disabilities have difficulty in successive processing and (2) the more severely impaired the children are in reading, the more impaired they are in successive processing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive processes involved in reading disability, and the implications of these cognitive deficits for the development of reading skills and the remediation of reading disabilities.
the identification of specific cognitive processes which are deficient in children with reading disabilities.
the cognitive processing abilities of children with learning disabilities
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PASS cognitive processing model provides an excellent framework for understanding the nature and treatment of reading disabilities.
reading disability is associated with deficits in successive processing, and that successive processing deficits may be a cause of reading disability.
the cognitive processing of children with reading disability is not uniform, but rather depends on the child's IQ level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reading disability is not a unitary phenomenon, but rather a collection of cognitive processing deficits.
reading disability can be understood in terms of cognitive processing deficits and that these deficits can be remediated.
the cognitive processing model provides a useful theoretical framework for the investigation of cognitive processing in reading disability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PASS cognitive processing model can help us to identify the specific cognitive processing weaknesses of children with reading disability.
cognitive processing measures can be used to understand and treat reading disability.
successive processing is a critical factor in the reading achievement of children with reading disability.
